limits: Verified never means interoperability with a device the design talks to unless a board measurement against that device is listed in the record; a design that checks its own output against its own model accepts its own symmetric mistakes.

Verified never means timing beyond the stated corner: a post-route timing result is for the part, speed grade, clock and tool version in its evidence file, not for other corners, temperatures or devices.

Verified never means beyond the widths and depths checked: a simulation covers the vectors it ran, a bounded formal result covers the stated depth only, and a per-width proof covers the widths it names; only a Lean proof marked all widths covers every width, and only for its model.

Verified never means the requirement is the right one: the text of a requirement is the human's check (or the planner's, where the record says delegated), and a record shows that checks exist and pass, not that nothing was left out.
Verified never means a hardware or board result unless a board measurement item is listed; a simulation is not the board.
Verified is about the files in the manifest at the hashes given. A change to any of them makes the record out of date (the CI check fails), and the evidence stale until it is re-recorded.
An agreement or acceptance recorded as delegated is the planner's decision on the owner's delegation, not a human sign-off; the record counts it apart.
name: atan2_mag
notes: Arithmetic library, function atan2_mag (brief 139d). Everything here is before Vivado: the model, the RTL variants, simulation, formal equivalence, Lean statements and the prepared out-of-context build files. No performance requirement exists because nothing about LUTs, DSPs, Fmax or power has been measured yet; the Vivado runs (build/<variant>/build.yaml) will add them. Every requirement is a draft written by the agent; none is agreed by a human. Lean statements are not approved. Generated by arith/tools/gen_testplan.py.

requirements.text: SymbiYosys with the slang front end compares each variant, delayed by its latency, with the exact function on 8 input bits to 24 fractional bits (a reference ROM written from the maths library, formal/*_ref.sv) and asserts the error stays within the bound of the job, which is the model's measured error at that point plus one unit for the reference's own rounding. A proof is by k-induction (for all inputs, any run length) at the widths in formal/jobs.yaml; wider points are covered by the exhaustive scan of the accuracy requirement and by simulation, not by proof. The quadrant map and the variants' structural identities are inside the checks.

item_views.title: A circular CORDIC step scales the squared length by a constant

requirements.source: arith/atan2_mag/rtl/atan2_cordic.sv (the x and y adders of one stage)
requirements.text: For every direction d = +-1 and every shift (scaled by u = 2^i), the step (u x - d y, u y + d x) multiplies x^2 + y^2 by exactly u^2 + 1, whatever the data: the CORDIC gain is a data-independent constant. The statement is the specification and is NOT approved by a human (verif/lean_approvals.yaml is empty), so the proof is shown but not counted as verification. The Lean text is a hand transcription of the RTL's structure; it models no timing or clocking.
